chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar and Burayd ibn Mu'awiyyah, from one of them (peace be upon them), who said:

"There is no harm in standing upon a prayer mat made of hair and wool if one prostrates upon the earth; but if it is from the plants of the earth, there is no harm in standing upon it and prostrating upon it."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about plaster (jiss) that is fired with excrement and bones of the dead, and with which the mosque is plastered; is prayer performed upon it? He wrote to me in his own hand: "Indeed, water and fire have purified it."

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, who said: Some of our companions wrote by the hand of Ibrahim ibn Uqbah to him, meaning Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), asking him about praying upon the Madani khurma (date palm mat). He wrote: "Pray in it if it is made with threads, and do not pray upon what is made with ropes." He said: So our companions hesitated, and I recited to them a verse of poetry from Ta'abbata Sharran al-Fahmi: 'As if it is the thread of Mariyy that is spun and twisted.' And Mariyy is a man who is a rope-maker who twists threads.

key_terms.الشَّعْر: Hair (animal hair, e.g., camel or goat)
key_terms.الْخُمْرَة: A type of mat made from date palm leaves

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on praying on mats made of hair, wool, or plants, and how is plaster purified?
ai.summary: These narrations from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* detail the jurisprudential criteria for prayer surfaces (*musalla*), emphasizing that impurities are removed by natural elements like water and fire, thereby validating plastered floors for prostration. The texts further distinguish between permissible fine-threaded mats and impermissible thick-rope mats, reflecting the Shia scholarly focus on the physical purity and structural integrity of the prayer space. This establishes a practical framework for believers to ensure their prostration is both ritually valid and physically grounded on pure earth or purified materials.
